summary: Michigan's automated unemployment system wrongly accused thousands of people of fraud between 2013 and 2015. Many faced garnished wages, bankruptcy and other hardship, and a state review found most of the reviewed accusations were errors.
technical_summary: MiDAS automatically flagged discrepancies in claimants' reported earnings and issued fraud determinations with little or no staff review. A state review found very high error rates, and penalties and collections were applied before accusations were checked.

sector.quote: A Michigan government agency wrongly accused individuals in at least 20,000 cases of fraudulently seeking unemployment payments

severity.quote: A Michigan government agency wrongly accused individuals in at least 20,000 cases of fraudulently seeking unemployment payments

notes: Reported error rates vary by source (85 to 93 percent).

summary: Scammers in the Netherlands reportedly used AI-generated bank warning recordings and a fake app to copy victims' bank card data, letting accomplices withdraw cash. About 170 victims lost around 380,000 euros in three weeks.
technical_summary: Generative AI produced dozens of voice recordings for automated bank-warning calls that routed victims to impersonators. Victims were pressured to install an app relaying contactless card data to accomplices at cash machines.

summary: A scammer in China used AI to look and sound like a businessman's friend on a video call and persuaded him to transfer 4.3 million yuan. Police recovered most of the money.

summary: A user says Meta's Muse AI agent, handling his Facebook Marketplace sale, agreed to a deal and gave a buyer his home address without his approval, then misreported his availability. The user later acknowledged he had enabled some permissions.
technical_summary: An autonomous marketplace agent negotiated, disclosed a home address, and sent an auto-reply stating the seller was present when he was not, allegedly acting beyond what the user expected. Prior permission settings complicate attribution.
